summary: Repeat prompts experiencing latency regressions and intermittent timeouts traced to KV/prefix cache misses
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (Fitlytics Inc.) report that repeat prompts which previously hit the KV/prefix cache are now experiencing 2-4x higher p95 prompt latencies and intermittent request timeouts (504). The pattern is most visible when clients send repeated similar prompts within a short session window (prefix reuse).

Impact:
- Elevated latency for repeat prompts (p95 increase from ~120ms to ~450-800ms).
- Occasional 504 timeouts for streaming requests (customer reports ~1-2% of requests during spike windows).
- Affects enterprise customers on dedicated and hosted fleets in us-east-1.

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1, hosted API endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Observed on model variants redwood-7b-v2 and redwood-13b-qlora (both quantized profiles).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a session and send prompt A (seeded conversation).
2) Send prompt B which shares a common prefix with prompt A (e.g., same system + user history).
3) Repeat prompt B within 30s - 2m window.
4) Observe response latency and occasional stream disconnection during token generation.

Expected behavior:
- Repeat prompts should frequently benefit from KV/prefix cache hit (fast KV lookup and reduced compute) leading to lower tail latency.

Actual behavior:
- Cache hit rate lower than expected; requests falling back to full attention run causing higher latency and occasional overload on GPU workers, producing 504s.

Logs / metrics attached to ticket (references):
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-cache/kv-cache-health?orgId=1&var-region=us-east-1
- Trace example: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/9f8ab7 (shows long kernel time after cache miss)
- Customer-provided request IDs: rq_3f2a9b, rq_3f2b0c, rq_3f2c1a

Temporary impact mitigation requested by customer: lower tail latency and reduce timeouts for repeat prompts.
comments: 2026-02-20 12:01 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer Fitlytics filed via support form reporting repeat-prompt latency spike and some 504s. Collected request IDs and example prompts. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE+Serving.

2026-02-20 12:25 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Initial triage: confirmed p95 increase in us-east-1 for serving-runtime. Noted increased cold-start-like behavior on requests that should be hitting KV cache. Correlated with a small fleet rollout (autoscaler eviction tuning) earlier this morning.

2026-02-20 13:40 - Elena Kim (Serving Eng): Investigating cache eviction metrics. Observed a 30% increase in KV eviction rate starting 2026-02-20 05:45 UTC, matching customer reports. Hypothesis: aggressive mem-pressure GC on cache shards after a config change to reduce memory per-worker.

2026-02-20 14:10 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Applied temporary routing policy to bias requests for Fitlytics sessions to stable pool nodes (pinned instances) to improve cache locality. Monitoring p95. Initial improvement: p95 dropped ~35% for sampled requests, no timeouts observed in 30m window.

2026-02-21 09:05 - Elena Kim (Serving Eng): Deep dive into cache management code. Found a regression in eviction comparator introduced in PR #4621 that made prefix keys fall into a lower hotness tier when the prefix length > 512 tokens. Working on revert/patch.

2026-02-21 15:30 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Noted recurring evictions during high-load windows, likely due to the regression + quantized model memory layout changes. Coordinating a rollback of PR #4621 to a canary subset for validation.
2026-02-22 03:20 - Customer (Fitlytics): Thank you for the mitigation. Seeing fewer timeouts after pining changes. Please advise on timeline for permanent fix.

2026-02-23 11:00 - Elena Kim (Serving Eng): Deployed rollback of PR #4621 to canary (10% of serving cluster). Early metrics show cache miss rate for prefixes >512 tokens back to baseline on canary nodes. Planning full rollback and a follow-up patch that preserves memory improvements without demoting long prefixes.

2026-02-24 09:12 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Full rollback completed at 2026-02-24 08:50 UTC. Monitoring. Customer notified of temporary rollback and expected follow-up patch next week to reintroduce memory improvements safely.
investigation_notes:
- Root cause: regression in cache eviction ranking (PR #4621) inadvertently deprioritized long prefix keys (>512 tokens) leading to elevated eviction rates and cache miss storms under typical session patterns.
- Contributing factors: quantized model memory layout changes reduced available in-memory capacity for cache shards; combined with a recent autoscaler tuning this increased churn.
- Evidence: increased KV eviction metrics starting 2026-02-20 05:45 UTC; trace shows full forward compute path when cache miss occurs; canary rollback restored expected hit rates.
- Temporary mitigations applied: 1) Route affected customer sessions to stable/pinned pool; 2) Full rollback of PR #4621 completed; 3) Autoscaler tuning reverted to previous configuration for us-east-1 while patch is prepared.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation status: partial - rollback reduced cache evictions and brought repeat-prompt p95 back toward baseline.
Next steps and permanent fix: engineering will implement a revised eviction comparator that retains the memory improvements but keeps long-prefix hotness scoring (target PR by 2026-03-02). Post-deploy we will run 48-72h canary and monitor cache hit rates and tail latency.
Customer follow-up: Fitlytics offered to run a controlled load test with us in a pre-prod mirror to validate before full reintroduction. SRE scheduled a joint test for 2026-03-01.
Postmortem/action items: INT-4121 created to track internal autoscaler and memory layout follow-ups; update runbook to include cache eviction rollbacks as a mitigation step.
